newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Idra presse share float to start July 9.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Idra presse share float to start July 9.

text.p: Italy's Idra Presse, a leading world maker of pressure casting machinery, plans a share float next month ahead of a bourse debut, sees good prospects of growth in the U.S. market and aims to make new acquisitions.

Senior managers of the Brescia-based group told a press presentation that its share offering, to take place on July 9 and 10, will be of 46.7 percent of its capital equal to 7.0 million shares at a price between 4,000 and 6,000 lire.
A listing on the Milan stock exchange will follow.
Idra expects 1997 turnover of 125 billion lire and a production value of around 130 billion, slightly up on 1996.
In the first quarter this year, it said gross operating margin rose to 10.7 percent from 8.8 percent for the full year of 1996, while return on sales was 8.5 percent against 6.7.
The company recently won an order from Chrysler worth around $30 million over three years which has opened a door to the U.S. market, Idra chairman Aldo Palma said.
Idra posted 1996 net profit of 4.16 billion lire against 3.6 billion in 1995. Some 51 percent of its turnover comes from European Union countries and 24 percent from Italy.
